scope: The 1834 box, whole: the forks, the main stem to the fort, the river turned south behind the baymouth spit to its natural outlet at Swearingen's half mile, the lake shore south of the outlet, and the ground south to the box floor at N -3800 - which takes in the Fort-to-Eighteenth-Street corridor the 1812 scene needs. South of Twelfth Street every vertex is conjectural, by the carried evidence limit; the battle ground is therefore modelled ground and is NOT a reconstruction from evidence, and this spec says so rather than letting the box's extent imply otherwise.
standard: No survey of this ground exists before Wright's of 1834, and no level of it before the 1850s. Every land elevation here is an 1835 dossier zone carried back twenty-three years, every planform line is a reading of 1834 with the works removed, and the lake stage of 1812 is not recorded at all. So nothing in this spec is better than `inferred`, every surface it AUTHORS for 1812 is `reconstructed`, and the generator must emit no land vertex `documented`.

notes: No lake stage of 1812 is recorded, and the dossier grades even the 1835 one conjectural (zone 2, 580 +/- 1.5 ft ASL). The water stands at the 1835 plane so the two epochs' ground can be compared and so every carried bank keeps the freeboard its zone gives it; the historic range of 576-582 ft ASL (dossier section 1.2) is the bound, Z -4 to +2. A lower 1812 lake would widen every beach and lower the river against its banks; a higher one would drown the spit, whose chosen crest is +4. Replaced by any stage reconstruction for the 1810s (NOAA/GLERL Michigan-Huron series).

notes: The 1834 bar's surface carried onto the 1812 spit, at the same +4 ft crest and 12 m face (1:9.8, zone 4's beach slope). Of the five reasons the 1834 spec gives for taking zone 7's LOW end, four hold for 1812 and one does not. Holding: the soldiers of Fort Dearborn trenched this bar with hand tools between 1816 and 1828, so it was low enough to dig through in the years after this scene; the 1839 Fort Dearborn Addition reading of the ground east of Michigan Avenue as 'at best... a low sandbar'; the direction of the error, because an 8 ft ridge here would hide the river behind a dune it never was; and the dossier's own zone 3 ridge at +9 to +10, which the young end of the same littoral system cannot equal. Not holding: the mid-1830s high-water phase, which is an 1835 fact. The 1812 stage is unknown (lake stage 1812), so it neither raises nor lowers the choice, and +4 stands on the other four. The planform is Wright's 1834 bar carried whole; over most of its length it is 108-164 m wide, wider than zone 7's 100-300 ft, and that is the trace's reading and is not narrowed here. The surface is emitted CONJECTURAL in the confidence channel: its shape is evidence, its height is not.

He says:' and sets the whole passage as a block quotation, which is why bk_mose1_019 - Benjamin Hall's 1830 arrival and the town's first tannery - is a reading of Blanchard through Moses and Kirkland and not of Moses and Kirkland. notes: South of Twelfth Street the 1812 ground was a flat plateau: every row from the beach's back (25 m inland) to 400 m inland read 9.4 ft (2.86 m), the South Division's carried plain, with no hill and no swale. Three readings say otherwise, and two of them are already in the 1812 evacuation readings data § landform, where the route of 15 August 1812 is drawn from them. Moses & Kirkland (1895, pp. 49-50) put 'the low wave-washed and wind-swept sand-hills' beginning at about Twelfth Street, with the shore flat north of it. The same book (p. 60) says 'the shore sand-hills were not high and not continuous', and that 'the surface of the bank, a hundred feet or more back from the water, varied from ten to twenty feet in height above its level'. Quaife (1913, p. 226) has 'a row of sand hills, or ridges, which ran between the prairie and the beach, parallel to the latter and distant from it about one hundred yards'. Dossier zone 5 sizes the fort's sand hills as hummocks 50-150 ft across with +10 to +14 ft peaks; its own source ("Fort Dearborn I." Chicagology, transcribing Chicago Magazine, March 1857, with…) is not cited here, because its rights are unresolved and nothing may be built from it (the project's rules rule 6), and no figure below rests on it alone. So the forms are built on the north lake dunes machinery (the terrain gen generator § the lakefront dunes), measured inland from the lake's edge, row by row. The bank's near face is a ridge centred 40 m (131 ft) back from the water. It stands +5.5 ft on the 9.4 ft plain, so its crests reach 14.9 ft. Quaife's row is a ridge centred at his hundred yards, 91.44 m, the figure the route's attack zone already uses. It stands +9.0 ft, so its crests reach 18.4 ft. Between them, at 64 m, is a swale up to 1.5 ft below the plain: the low wet ground behind a foredune where a sand prairie stands. Hummock noise breaks every ridge into hills 20-40 m across, inside zone 5's 50-150 ft, because the hills were 'not continuous'. Where the noise lets a ridge down, the ground is the plain's own 9.4 ft. That is 0.6 ft under M&K's low figure and inside lake stage 1812's own -4 to +2 ft uncertainty, so their ten-to-twenty is met by the hills and not forced onto every cell. The beach (the bank face, 25 m) is left as it was, so the column's route on the waterline keeps its ground. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: every position, height and width. The readings fix that the hills existed, where they began, roughly how far back they stood and how high the bank rose, and they place no single hill. THE DISAGREEMENT IS KEPT, NOT RECONCILED: Quaife starts the ridges at the river mouth, 1.6 km north of M&K's Twelfth Street. North of Twelfth the carried 1834 south lake dunes reach (N -700 to -2120, L334, built on dossier zone 5's 'white sand hills both to the north and south' of the fort) already stands, and this block adds nothing there. The north end therefore fades in over the 60 m south of the evidence limit line, and the south end runs past the box floor so it does not fade inside the box. Admitted in the liberties register L392.

notes: Other work, on the owner's report (2026-11-06) that the bank the accounts describe 'does not really seem to show here from the land' and should be 'much more significant and accurate'. Other work's sand hills south of Twelfth and the carried 1834 dunes north of it stood +2 to +9 ft on the 9 ft plain, broken into hummocks, behind a 20 m ramp from the water: from the beach, nothing to charge up. Heald's report gives the shape and the distance: the column took 'the beach, with the lake on our left, and a high sand bank on our right, at about 100 yards distance', the attackers waited 'behind the bank', and his men 'marched up... to the top of the bank'. Wau-Bun has 'a range of sand-hills intervening between the prairie and the beach', 'charged up the bank', and behind it 'a sort of ravine, intervening between the sand-banks and the prairie' in which the attackers 'had concealed themselves'; Mrs. Helm was led 'up the sand-banks' through deep sand; Wentworth's Heald family account has a 'bluff'. Moses & Kirkland give the height: the bank's surface 'a hundred feet or more back from the water' and 'ten to twenty feet' above it. Quaife, from Heald, puts 'a row of sand hills, or ridges' 'about one hundred yards' from the beach. So the ground along Heald's band is laid as one profile measured inland from the lake's edge, row by row: a beach of 26 m rising to 2.6 ft, the column's road and wide enough for its wagons; the bank's near face, climbing from 2.6 ft at 26 m to 13 ft at 38 m, about 25 degrees, under the angle at which dry sand stands, so the bank's surface stands 14.5 ft high from 44 m (M&K's 'a hundred feet or more' is 30.5 m); the sand hills rising behind it to Heald's high bank, a crest of 19 ft at 96 m, his hundred yards being 91.44 m; their back falling through 12.5 ft at 120 m into the ravine, 4.6 ft at 144 m, four feet under the prairie it opens onto; and the plain's own 8.5 ft by 200 m, where the ground already there takes over across 185-215 m. Hummocks of up to 3 ft play across the hills only (32-124 m), clipped at M&K's 20 ft, so the tops range across their ten to twenty and the troughs between them let the line down ('not continuous'). The block runs N -1300 to -2700 with 220 m fades, covering Heald's band (the 1812 evacuation route data, N -1456 to -2192 along the shore) and the reach where the accounts' sand hills begin, and replaces the hummock fields of south lake dunes and south lake sand hills 1812 where it stands. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: every width, height and place in the profile, the hummocks, and the ravine's depth; the readings fix that a beach, a high bank of sand hills and a ravine stood in that order, how far back and how high the bank stood, and nothing places one hill. Where the sand hills BEGAN is still disagreed (Quaife: at the river mouth; M&K: about Twelfth Street) and this block does not settle it. Admitted in the liberties register L-other work-battle-shore-1812. Other work (owner, 2026-11-07, after the battle-site research): the block now runs N -3650 to -1300, so the same beach, bank, ridges and ravine carry on south past Eighteenth Street (N -3207) to about Twentieth, where the accounts that name a place put the fight: the Kinzie family's two cottonwoods in Eighteenth Street and Arnold's 'near the place where the attack began' (Andreas 1884 p. 31), Fernando Jones's burial ground at Seventeenth and Prairie and the grave with U.S. buttons at Twenty-first and Indiana (Kirkland 1893), and Heald's own journal, 'two miles from the Fort' (Quaife 1913 App. III). North of N -2480 nothing moves: the profile, the hummock and wander noise are seeded on absolute coordinates, so the ground other work laid along Heald's mile and a half is kept as built, by the owner's ruling ('keep that beachy sandy shore and elevations and ridges along there that you already built'). Only the old south fade (N -2700 to -2480) becomes full bank. Admitted in the liberties register L-other work-battle-shore-1812 (revised).

notes: Other work, on the owner's question at stop 10 (2026-11-06): 'where on the open prairie is the small elevation? you should attempt to cite it and place it'. Heald names it, in the report written ten weeks after: 'a small elevation in the open prarie, out of shot of the bank or any other cover', with the attackers left 'on the top of the bank' and Heald walking out to them alone. Wau-Bun's account (Mrs. Helm, from memory) has the survivors 'gaining a rising ground, not far from the Oak Woods'; Quaife repeats Heald; Moses & Kirkland read it as 'far inland, out of gun-shot from the bank'. No account gives a distance or a size and none locates the Oak Woods, so it is placed by the three things they do say. (1) Along the march: at Heald's own 'about a mile and a half', the station the 1812 evacuation route data derives at E +1318, N -1853, because the withdrawal was out of the fight at the bank and Heald was not followed. (2) Inland, due west of it on the same row, the direction away from the lake. (3) Out of shot: the high bank's crest stands at Heald's hundred yards and its back falls to the ravine by about 125 m from the water (battle bank 1812), and the rise's centre is put 358 m from the water, about 230 m (250 yards) beyond the back of the bank, past the range at which a smooth-bore musket of 1812 could be aimed at a man; that range is this project's reasoning and cites nothing. Its size is 'small': a top 36 m across, room for the 'few men' left, standing 8 ft over the plain, with a 34 m skirt, so it is a rise on the plain and not a hill. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: its place, its height and its size; its existence is attested by the commander who stood on it. Admitted in the liberties register L-other work-battle-shore-1812. Other work (owner's choice, 2026-11-07, after the battle-site research): MOVED from E +960, N -1853 to E +1215, N -3420, between the later Nineteenth and Twentieth Streets near Indiana Avenue. (1) Along the march: the place readings put the attack at Eighteenth Street (the Kinzie family's cottonwoods; Arnold, from the Kinzies, 'near the place where the attack began'), and Heald's journal gives 'two miles from the Fort'; Heald's report's 'about a mile and a half' is the one figure that falls short of them. (2) Direction: Arnold has the fight moving 'south and west', Wau-Bun has the rising ground 'not far from the Oak Woods', which Kirkland (1893) puts at Hyde Park, to the south, and Fernando Jones's vidette grave at Twenty-first and Indiana lay 'southwest of the massacre-ground'; so it is put south-west of the Eighteenth Street bank, not due west. (3) Out of shot: 377 m from the water on its row (the shore stands at E +1592 there), about 230 m beyond the back of the bank, the same allowance as before. Its height and size are unchanged. The rise other work built at the old place is kept as ground, by the owner's ruling, as tenth street rise 1812.

notes: Other work, on the owner's ruling of 2026-11-08, flying the Potawatomi camps from the air: 'There would be more water in that slough they are gathering around can you make sure though sloughs are carved correctly and naturally with the right water there'. THE ROUTE IS THE 1835 ONE: the same documented course ("Wolf's Point and the Town of Chicago." Chicagology: it drained the public-square pond and the Wells Street marsh, 'passed over the site of the Tremont House and entered the river at the end of State Street'; Conley/Stelzer 1933's winding line; Wright 1834's traced notch for the mouth), the 1834 spec's state slough course and state slough mouth vertices joined into one line. THE WATER IS THE OWNER'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: zone 14 reads the bed +0.5 to +1.5 ft above the 1835 water, a damp drain in July 1835, and that reading stays on the 1835 ground. No 1812 stage or depth is recorded (lake stage 1812). For 1812 the bed is carved below the water plane from about 75 m below the head to the river, so the slough holds open water through the camps: pools to about -1.8 ft and narrows (never below -1.95 ft: a slough stays shallower than the -0.60 m the flora's divisions take for river channel, the walkthrough's trees code channel y), a profile of [along (m), bed (ft), water half (m), margin (m)] knots, each modulated +/-30% by seeded noise so no two reaches match. CARVED AS A WATERCOURSE, NOT A DITCH: the centreline winds up to 6 m off the documented line (inside Conley's 20-30 m reading tolerance), never in the last 100 m, which keep Wright's notch; water edge, then a wet margin rising 0.8 ft (3-3.5 m wide through the camps, under a metre where the mouth cuts the State Street ridge toe to Wright's notch), then the bank at 1.2 ft per metre into the plain, the ground only ever lowered. The head stays a damp hollow above the water and feathers out east of Clark. Where the water would reach a camp's site outline the line bends round it (never in the last 35 m, Wright's notch), and the bank may lower a site's ground by no more than 0.4 ft; the carve may not touch the ground under any lodge, hearth, arbor or picket of the camps (terrain gen e1830 state slough, which refuses). Recorded in the liberties register (L-other work-state-slough-1812).

notes: Other work, on the owner's ruling of 2026-11-08 ('make sure those sloughs are carved correctly and naturally with the right water there'). THE COURSE IS WRIGHT'S: the centreline is hydrology.geojson's north side slough, read whole off the NA/HUP sheet by other work to 1.78 m median, so it does not wind off its trace (meander 0). WHAT CHANGES FOR 1812 is the section. The 1834 watercourses entry floods a constant 7.1 m band to -1.0 ft and stops square at its head. Here the slough is a still backwater ('marshy, wet areas with little current', the form the 1834 record cites): water from about 25 m below the head to the river, its half-width read round other work's stroke separation (13.0 m median, 7-23 m) at 2 to 5.5 m, varied +/-30% into pools and narrows, a bed of -0.5 to about -1.7 ft, never below -1.95 ft (the walkthrough's trees code channel y) (the 1834 entry's -1.0 is invented too), a wet margin rising 0.8 ft, then the bank at 1.2 ft per metre; the head a damp hollow that feathers into the plain. Every depth and width here is reconstructed. Recorded in the liberties register (L-other work-state-slough-1812). Cited to zone 19, the North Division ground it is cut into: the dossier gives the slough no row of its own.
